LESSON MENU
IC REGULATOR OPERATION
The purpose of this lesson is to show the operation of an IC Regulator, and how it may be put in place of a Multi-component Regulator.
DISCUSSION
The IC Regulator has many special features which make it extremely safe and durable.
Most IC Regulators have thermal overload protection and internal short-circuit current limiting protection so that there is virtually no risk of overload.
XUUIUIUII
The following is a block diagram of the power supply that we will be working with.
The whole circuit is actually a 12 VDC power supply, but we will mainly be directing our attention to the regulator.
The first block is simply the AC input to the rectifier.
Next we have a bridge rectifier, it changes the applied AC to a full wave pulsating DC. The DC voltage has half the applied voltage value.
This pulsating DC is then sent through a filter capacitor and smoothed to an almost constant DC.
The filtered DC is sent through the regulator and kept at a constant 12 VDC level. This voltage is then applied to the load.'
There are many different kinds of regulators, we will discuss the 7812 IC regulator.
This regulator will maintain a constant 12 VDC output when the input is between 14.5 and 30 V.

OUTPUT CURRENT - The 7812 voltage regulator produces a constant 12 VDC output at 1.5 Amps with an 8 ohm load connected to its output. Anything under 8 ohms would draw more than 1.5 amps. The IC regulator would become very hot and the thermal protection would engage.
When dealing with a limited area or many parts, an IC regulator can be very useful in conserving space.
When in the field, troubleshooting an IC regulator is easy.
